{{Short description|Open problem in symbolic dynamics}}

'''Nivat's conjecture''' is an open problem in [[symbolic dynamics]] and [[combinatorics on words]] concerning the relationship between local pattern complexity and global periodicity in two-dimensional configurations. Proposed by French computer scientist [[Maurice Nivat]] at the 1997 [[International Colloquium on Automata, Languages and Programming]] (ICALP), it is a two-dimensional analogue of the [[Morse–Hedlund theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Kari
 |first1=Jarkko
 |last2=Moutot
 |first2=Etienne
 |title=Nivat's conjecture and pattern complexity in algebraic subshifts
 |journal=Theoretical Computer Science
 |volume=777
 |pages=379–386
 |year=2019
 |doi=10.1016/j.tcs.2018.12.029
}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
 |last=Boyle
 |first=Mike
 |chapter=Open problems in symbolic dynamics
 |title=Dynamics and Randomness II
 |series=Contemporary Mathematics
 |volume=469
 |publisher=American Mathematical Society
 |year=2008
 |pages=69–118
 |doi=10.1090/conm/469/09161
}}</ref>

== Statement ==
Let <math>A</math> be a finite [[alphabet (formal languages)|alphabet]] and let <math>x\colon\mathbb{Z}^2\to A</math> be a two-dimensional configuration. For positive integers <math>n</math> and <math>m</math>, let <math>P_x(n,m)</math> be the number of distinct <math>n\times m</math> rectangular patterns that occur in <math>x</math>. The configuration is called periodic if there is a nonzero vector <math>v\in\mathbb{Z}^2</math> such that <math>x(u+v)=x(u)</math> for every <math>u\in\mathbb{Z}^2</math>.<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Kari
 |first1=Jarkko
 |last2=Moutot
 |first2=Etienne
 |title=Decidability and Periodicity of Low Complexity Tilings
 |journal=Theory of Computing Systems
 |volume=67
 |pages=125–148
 |year=2023
 |doi=10.1007/s00224-021-10063-8
}}</ref>

Nivat's conjecture states that if there exist positive integers <math>n,m</math> such that
:<math>P_x(n,m)\le nm,</math>
then <math>x</math> is periodic.<ref name="Boyle2008">{{cite book
 |last=Boyle
 |first=Mike
 |chapter=Open problems in symbolic dynamics
 |title=Dynamics and Randomness II
 |series=Contemporary Mathematics
 |volume=469
 |publisher=American Mathematical Society
 |year=2008
 |pages=69–118
 |doi=10.1090/conm/469/09161
}}</ref>

== Partial results ==
Several weaker forms and special cases of the conjecture have been proved. Quas and Zamboni proved periodicity under the stronger bound <math>P_x(n,m)\le nm/16</math>.<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Quas
 |first1=Anthony
 |last2=Zamboni
 |first2=Luca Q.
 |title=Periodicity and local complexity
 |journal=Theoretical Computer Science
 |volume=319
 |issue=1–3
 |pages=229–240
 |year=2004
 |doi=10.1016/j.tcs.2004.02.026
}}</ref> Cyr and Kra later proved periodicity under the bound <math>P_x(n,m)\le nm/2</math>.<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Cyr
 |first1=Van
 |last2=Kra
 |first2=Bryna
 |title=Nonexpansive Z²-subdynamics and Nivat's conjecture
 |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
 |volume=367
 |issue=9
 |pages=6487–6537
 |year=2015
 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-2015-06391-0
}}</ref>

For rectangles of fixed small height, Sander and Tijdeman proved the conjecture for height at most 2, and Cyr and Kra extended this to height at most 3.<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Cyr
 |first1=Van
 |last2=Kra
 |first2=Bryna
 |title=Complexity of short rectangles and periodicity
 |journal=European Journal of Combinatorics
 |volume=52
 |pages=146–173
 |year=2016
 |doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2015.10.003
}}</ref> Kari and Moutot proved that the conjecture holds for uniformly recurrent configurations.<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Kari
 |first1=Jarkko
 |last2=Moutot
 |first2=Etienne
 |title=Decidability and Periodicity of Low Complexity Tilings
 |journal=Theory of Computing Systems
 |volume=67
 |pages=125–148
 |year=2023
 |doi=10.1007/s00224-021-10063-8
}}</ref>
